text:
Sasha (Support): heads-up — customer (AcmePayments) reported massive p99 regressions on streaming responses since Friday deploy. TTFB looks ok for most calls but total time is spiking, a lot of chunks delayed. hitting them in production, escalated from support.

Debi (Support): saw the ticket, they pasted a couple examples where a 2s TTFB then a 6–10s gap before the next chunks. they say non-streaming requests don't show the same tail.

Sasha (Support): repro steps they sent (sanitized):
```
# streaming curl
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-stream","prompt":"long output test","max_tokens":800}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```
They also tried SDK streaming and see same gaps.

Mike (Eng): thanks — first guess: chunk coalescing/flush heuristic landed in runtime last week (PR #512). It batches small writes to reduce syscalls which lowers cost but can introduce tail latency if flush timer is too long for low throughput streams.

Ana (ML): can we confirm if the runtime changed default flush interval or the coalescing threshold? I remember a change to prefer 4ms coalesce window on GPUs. If some clients produce bursts then long idle, timer could pile up and produce 50–200ms extra per chunk. But reported gaps of seconds suggests maybe fallback path that increases timer to 1s under low throughput.

Kevin (Oncall): grabbing traces from the customer example. attaching logs and trace id: trace=tr_9ab3... we see streaming frames emitted, then a `FLUSH_DELAY` event at server side with duration ~1200ms.

Sasha (Support): paste from their logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-11T18:42:13Z] STREAM_FRAME_SENT seq=1 size=1024
[2026-03-11T18:42:15Z] STREAM_FRAME_SENT seq=2 size=2048
[2026-03-11T18:42:16Z] FLUSH_DELAY duration_ms=1234 reason="coalesce_timer"
[2026-03-11T18:42:17Z] STREAM_FRAME_SENT seq=3 size=512
```

Debi (Support): customer says p95 ~450ms (ok) but p99 jumps to 5–12s for streaming only. They rely on streaming for progressive UX.

Mike (Eng): reprod locally against canary runtime with our perf harness. I can reproduce tail events when output token rate low. Non-streaming path is unaffected because server buffers until completion. So this is definitely flush/coalesce related.

Ana (ML): risk assessment: changing flush policy to immediate will reduce tail latency but increase egress syscalls and could raise CPU and token cost by ~2–4% for small-chunk workloads. For high-throughput customers it's probably negligible.

Kevin (Oncall): quick mitigation options:
- customer can set header `X-Redwood-Stream-Flush: immediate` to force no coalescing (server honors it).
- recommend using non-streaming endpoint for large long-running generations until we patch.
- we can hotfix runtime to reduce timer from 1000ms -> 50ms in canary.

Sasha (Support): sent customer steps for header workaround and asked them to try canary endpoint. they confirmed header improved tail in a few test calls.

Debi (Support): customer wants a more permanent fix. they use Dedicated and will want a config toggle in their Dedicated cluster so they can control flush granularity.

Mike (Eng): propose rollout plan:
1) revert aggressive coalescing in mainline and push hotfix to canary (reduce timer to 50ms, keep coalesce window but limit max delay).
2) add per-tenant config `stream.flush_mode` with options `auto|immediate|coalesce` and an override header.
3) add metric `stream.chunk_delay_ms{tenant}` and an alert for p99 > 500ms.

Ana (ML): also add an acceptance test in perf harness that simulates low token-rate streams and asserts p99 < 800ms.

Kevin (Oncall): deploying hotfix to canary now — patch v2.4.3-hotfix. will monitor.

deploy-bot: release v2.4.3-hotfix deployed to canary (canary=10%): image rwd/runtime:v2.4.3-hotfix — started 2026-03-12T03:14:00Z

Mike (Eng): canary metrics (10 min after deploy): stream.chunk_delay_ms p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 110ms for sampled tenant traffic. p95 unchanged. CPU overhead +1.3% on canary nodes.

Sasha (Support): passed results to customer. they ran a few long tests and said UX noticeably better.

Debi (Support): customer asked for ETA on main rollout and Dedicated config.

Mike (Eng): ETA: if canary stays green for 24h we'll roll to prod in staged ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) over next 48h. Dedicated config will be in next release (v2.5.0) with a tenant flag we can flip.

Ana (ML): followups for backlog:
- docs: streaming best-practices + header (example curl)
- perf test added to CI harness
- dashboard tile for stream.chunk_delay_ms and p99 heatmap

Sasha (Support): adding KB link in ticket with workaround, timeline, and note on possible cost impact for immediate flush.

Kevin (Oncall): added temporary alert to staging: ALERT StreamChunkDelayHigh if avg(p99(stream.chunk_delay_ms), 5m) > 500ms.

Mike (Eng): technical note for release: the offending change was PR #512 — coalesce timer default `max_coalesce_ms=1000` meant low-throughput streams could wait up to 1s. we changed to `max_coalesce_ms=50` with `min_coalesce_ms=0` and added tenant override via config.

Debi (Support): customer ok with staged rollout and will accept the header as interim. they asked us to confirm Dedicated configuration before they sign next quarter contract.

Sasha (Support): closing loop — will update ticket after prod ramp. planned tasks: docs + KB + dedicated-flag + perf test. assigning followups to @Mike and @Ana.

Mike (Eng): noted. I'll open the release PR and the tenant-config PR now.

Ana (ML): I'll add the perf scenario and evaluate cost tradeoffs for various flush settings.

Kevin (Oncall): leaving this thread open for 24h monitoring, will post final prod numbers.

Sasha (Support): thanks everyone. tagging for visibility: @Mike (Eng) @Ana (ML) @Kevin (Oncall) @Debi (Support). :thumbsup:
